parties: Sangita Biyani acquirer; Praxis Home Retail Limited target
headline: Sangita Biyani files SEBI Regulation 31(4) substantial acquisition disclosure in Praxis Home Retail
sum: Sangita Biyani has triggered mandatory SEBI Regulation 31(4) disclosure following substantial acquisition of shares in publicly listed Praxis Home Retail Limited. The filing indicates a cross-threshold shareholding event requiring immediate public notice under the Takeover Code.
implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosure marks the entry point for takeover scrutiny; if acquisition moves toward 25% or more, open offer obligations crystallize—partners should immediately audit current shareholder register, lock-in periods, and competing acquirer pre-emption rights.
detail: Sangita Biyani, the disclosing acquirer, has filed a Regulation 31(4) notice with NSE marking a substantial share acquisition in Praxis Home Retail Limited (a NSE-listed consumer retail company). The filing triggers mandatory disclosure obligations under the SEBI Takeover Regulations whenever shareholding crosses specified thresholds (typically 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25% etc.). The exact quantum of shares acquired, the purchase price, transaction date, and Biyani's precise post-transaction shareholding percentage are not disclosed in the available Bar & Bench primary source; corroboration from NSE disclosures or company announcements is required to establish deal value and structure.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 – Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure by acquirer upon crossing specified shareholding thresholds; triggers public notice and 2-working-day window to announce open offer if 25%+ threshold breached.

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011 – Regulation 3, 4 (definitions and applicability)
framework.note: Sets scope of 'acquirer', 'target', and transactions subject to takeover code; excludes small acquisitions and off-market permissioned deals.

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011 – Regulation 10 (open offer triggers)
framework.note: If acquisition results in 25% or higher shareholding, mandatory open offer at highest price paid in preceding 12 months required.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) (Amendment) Regulations, 2024
framework.note: Recent amendments may modify disclosure timelines, exemptions, or open-offer pricing; review current text.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013 – Section 91 (disclosure of beneficial ownership)
framework.note: Complements SEBI disclosure; acquirer must disclose ultimate beneficial owner if nominee/trust structure used.
Praxis Home Retail must make simultaneous disclosures to stock exchange; governs target-side timing and content.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 – Section 29A (if applicable)
framework.note: Restricts certain acquirers (related parties, defaulters) from acquiring control; audit if Sangita Biyani or related persons have prior insolvency history.

conditions: Shareholding must cross one of the specified thresholds (5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%) triggering Regulation 31(4) disclosure
approvals: Open offer approval by SEBI if 25%+ threshold crossed (conditional)
Target board/shareholder approval if open offer triggered (conditional)
structure.novel: Standard SEBI takeover disclosure process; no novelty reported.

triggers.note: Acquirer must file disclosure within 2 trading days of acquiring shares that cross threshold; NSE publishes notice to market.
If shareholding reaches 25% or more, open offer at highest price in preceding 12 months becomes mandatory within 4 weeks.
Target company must simultaneously announce receipt of disclosure notice to market and to shareholders.
